tier_reason: PR #1375 (merged 2023-05-07) gives only the author's hedged statement of an average 6X-7X latency gain for vectorUnpackX over the scalar plainUnpackLongs in a 'functional micro-performance test'; no CPU model, compiler, flags, per-width data or timing harness are published (c++/test/TestRleVectorDecoder.cc is a correctness test with no timing code). First-party numbers without methodology are tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: PR author: 'In the funcational micro-performance test I suppose AVX-512 vector decode could bring average 6X ~ 7X performance latency improvement compare vector function vectorUnpackX with the original Rle-bit-packing decode function plainUnpackLongs.' No per-bit-width data is given.
corrections.baseline: ORC C++ scalar RLEv2 bit-packing decoder (plainUnpackLongs, pre-change)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated. CMake option -DBUILD_ENABLE_AVX512=ON (default OFF); runtime override via ORC_USER_SIMD_LEVEL=AVX512 or none
corrections.hardware: Intel SKX (Skylake-SP/X) or newer AVX-512 platform per the PR text; exact CPU model not stated
corrections.caveats: First-party PR claim, hedged by the author ('I suppose'), from a micro-benchmark that is not in the repository, with no CPU model, compiler or flags. A ClickHouse contributor (taiyang-li) tested a 505 MB, 1.2M-row ORC file in the PR thread and saw no measurable improvement; the author suggested gains may appear only for non-aligned bit widths. Blocks smaller than 512 bits fall back to scalar decoding. AVX-512 path is off by default at build time. Baseline is ORC's own scalar decoder, not varint, Simple8b or FastPFor. Merged 2023-05-07; a RISC-V Vector (RVV) bit-unpacking path for RLEv2 (ORC-2216) was committed on 2026-09-21.

notes: Catalog rule: apache/orc is on data/known_list.txt only because merging this record put it there (commit e5783ba, 'Wave 9: merge w9-intpack-registry'); no earlier wave lists ORC as an entry (wave 6 mentions it only as a BtrBlocks baseline), so there is nothing to fold into. Recommend keeping it as the single entry for Apache ORC's C++ reader (RLEv2 SIMD bit-unpacking, now AVX-512 and RVV) under the repo id; later ORC findings should fold into it as evidence.
